name: Lenient Vertex Cover
description: You are given a simple connected undirected graph, consisting of $$$n$$$ vertices and $$$m$$$ edges. The vertices are numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$. A vertex cover of a graph is a set of vertices such that each edge has at least one of its endpoints in the set. Let's call a lenient vertex cover such a vertex cover that at most one edge in it has both endpoints in the set. Find a lenient vertex cover of a graph or report that there is none. If there are multiple answers, then print any of them.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of testcases. The first line of each testcase contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$m$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^6$$$; $$$n - 1 \le m \le \min(10^6, \frac{n \cdot (n - 1)}{2})$$$) — the number of vertices and the number of edges of the graph. Each of the next $$$m$$$ lines contains two integers $$$v$$$ and $$$u$$$ ($$$1 \le v, u \le n$$$; $$$v \neq u$$$) — the descriptions of the edges. For each testcase, the graph is connected and doesn't have multiple edges. The sum of $$$n$$$ over all testcases doesn't exceed $$$10^6$$$. The sum of $$$m$$$ over all testcases doesn't exceed $$$10^6$$$.
output_specification: For each testcase, the first line should contain YES if a lenient vertex cover exists, and NO otherwise. If it exists, the second line should contain a binary string $$$s$$$ of length $$$n$$$, where $$$s_i = 1$$$ means that vertex $$$i$$$ is in the vertex cover, and $$$s_i = 0$$$ means that vertex $$$i$$$ isn't. If there are multiple answers, then print any of them.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1680F — Lenient Vertex Cover [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
